headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from gpt-researcher feeding pdf.js, with low direct leakage/conflict due to pdf.js no-egress design.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher ingests web/research content and can call MCP, while pdf.js parses PDF content in a browser-based worker. If gpt-researcher’s output is passed into pdf.js or vice versa through a shared workspace, attacker-controlled document text could be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher writes untrusted text into a shared PDF or markdown workspace that pdf.js opens
IF pdf.js output is re-ingested by gpt-researcher as instructions without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate input and output folders for the two agents
Disable automatic re-ingestion of generated PDFs/text
Add a provenance header to every handoff file
Review any PDF text before it is treated as instructions
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and trust boundaries in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher can read local documents and send data to external APIs, but pdf.js has network egress none and only handles PDF files. The main leakage path is one-way from shared files into gpt-researcher’s backend, not from pdf.js. Because no shared workspace is documented, this remains a limited, configuration-dependent risk.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory containing sensitive PDFs
IF gpt-researcher uploads those files to external APIs during research
mitigations: Store sensitive PDFs outside the shared workspace
Run gpt-researcher on redacted copies only
Confirm pdf.js is used offline with no network access
Restrict API keys for gpt-researcher during sensitive runs
requires-engineering: add per-folder access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, but only gpt-researcher has broad filesystem and network egress; pdf.js is browser-based with no egress. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write surface, so direct write-write conflict is not evident. Uncertainty is limited because the profiles do not show a common writable target.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same output directory
IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes through one orchestrator process
Use read-only mounts for pdf.js
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
requires-engineering: add locking for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations, and pdf.js can render or process PDFs that may contain those outputs. If pdf.js consumes gpt-researcher’s generated content without verification, formatting or factual errors can cascade into downstream documents. The pair lacks a built-in verification step in the profiles, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF pdf.js is used to render or distribute PDFs generated from gpt-researcher output
IF no human or automated verification step checks the generated research before publication
mitigations: Add a review step before PDF publication
Compare claims against source citations manually
Mark generated PDFs as draft until approved
Keep source documents separate from generated reports
requires-engineering: add automated citation validation

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher handles secrets and broad external APIs, while pdf.js is local-only and touches PDF documents. No residency or certification mismatch is documented in the profiles, so compliance risk is mainly about accidental routing of sensitive PDFs into gpt-researcher’s external services. The other agent is not cited for residency because it has no egress and no secrets handling.
conditions: IF sensitive or regulated PDFs are sent from pdf.js into gpt-researcher for analysis
IF those documents are processed by external APIs without a DPA or retention review
mitigations: Classify PDFs before sending them to gpt-researcher
Use a local-only mode for regulated documents
Confirm retention settings on external APIs
Keep compliance-sensitive files out of the research workflow
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by document class
